fetchFlights.notes: History q matches ICAO, callsign, or flight id. since/until are unix seconds on end_time. History limit is capped at 200 and skip at 10000.

fetchTelemetry.notes: Live and history responses hold at most limit points (default 5000, max 20000): the newest ones, or with since > 0 the oldest ones after since. The response carries truncated: true beside data when points were left out.

subscribe.notes: Limit which /ws/live streams this connection receives. Omit or pass [] for the default set (flights, alerts, telemetry, stats). Raw frames are not a live stream; connect to /ws/raw (JSON) or /ws/beast / the Beast TCP port (dump1090 binary) instead.

beast.format: dump1090 Beast binary (0x1a type + 6-byte 12 MHz clock + signal byte + Mode S payload, 0x1a escaped). Frames are merged across receivers (stronger RSSI; Hamming vote only for the same DF/ICAO). Outbound clock is engine receive time so receivers share one time base.

client_request.action: fetchFlights | fetchFlight | fetchTelemetry | fetchAlerts | fetchStats | fetchZones | fetchConfig | subscribe

connect: Open /ws/live, read the hello + snapshot (flights, alerts, stats), then either listen for pushed streams or send type=request messages. Optional /ws/live?streams=flights,alerts limits the initial set. Corrected Mode S frames are pushed as JSON on /ws/raw ({"type": "raw", "frames": [...]}, no handshake) and re-encoded as dump1090 Beast binary on /ws/beast (binary WebSocket) and, when web.beast_port is set, a TCP listener compatible with OpenSky Network's feeder (BEASTHOST/BEASTPORT, default port 30105; dump1090 itself uses 30005, which the engine reads). Raw and Beast are not /ws/live subscribe streams.

shape.code: bad_request | not_found | rate_limited | history_unavailable | live_unavailable | internal_error

raw.format: JSON text {"type": "raw", "frames": [...]} using the live:raw payload dicts as-is (hex, timestamp, receiver, receivers, rssi, clock, df, icao). No handshake, RPC, or ping.

streams.alerts: Live alert episodes for currently tracked flights. Pushed snapshots hold every active episode plus the newest inactive ones, at least 50 in total when available (max(50, active count)); fetchAlerts is the full list.
streams.flights: Full live flight list whenever positions or alerts change.
streams.stats: live_flights / active_alerts / retained_flights / historical_alerts, plus redis / history booleans, engine_seen_at (unix seconds, or null if the tracking engine is not writing a heartbeat) and engine_live (server-side heartbeat freshness check).
streams.telemetry: New track points since the client last received telemetry.
